title: Where things belong: OneDrive, Teams, SharePoint, email
goal: Every employee knows where a document belongs and how to share it, so nothing important stays only in OneDrive.
summary: This policy tells every employee where each document belongs, how to share it, and what to do before leaving a project or the company. It is binding for all Microsoft 365 users in the company and is published unchanged on the intranet. The goal is for every document to have one place and one owner, and to be found by everyone who needs it.

sections.title: 1. Purpose and scope
sections.html:
1. Purpose and scope

You save every document created in the company somewhere. If it ends up in OneDrive, only you see it. If you send it as an attachment, two versions come into being. If you save it to your desktop, it disappears along with a lost laptop. This policy determines where each document belongs, how to share it, and what to do before leaving a project or the company.

The policy applies to all employees and contractors with a company account and to all documents, notes, and messages. The rules for sharing outside the company are in GOV-10 External sharing and guests, retention periods in GOV-12 Retention, archiving and disposal, and working with libraries for site owners in GOV-07 Content and document management.

sections.title: 2. Rules
sections.html:
2. Rules

Location matrix:

LocationWhat belongs thereFor whomHow long
OneDrivePersonal and work-in-progress documents, drafts, notes for myselfOnly me; at most a small circle of colleagues for a limited timeTemporarily; after completion, move to the right place
Teams channelTeam work, project and team files, ongoing collaborationMembers of the team or channelFor the duration of the project or the team's activity
SharePoint site (department, intranet)Official, approved, and long-term documents: policies, contracts, templates, minutesThe department or the whole companyLong-term, according to retention periods
Loop, OneNoteMeeting notes, working lists, ideas in progressMe and my collaboratorsWhile they are live; conclusions are transcribed into a document
EmailCommunication and agreements; a document is sent as a linkRecipientsCommunication yes, storage no
Local drive, USB, private cloudsNothing–Prohibited
  • P-08-01Basic Nothing important stays only in OneDrive. A document that others need or that is to remain after the work is finished is moved to a Teams channel or a SharePoint site.
  • P-08-02Basic A link is shared, not an attachment. An attachment is sent only to recipients outside the company's Microsoft 365 and only for Public or Internal documents.
  • P-08-03Basic A document has one owner and lives in one place. Copies to another site, OneDrive, or email are not created; whoever needs a working version works in the original document.
  • P-08-04Basic Confidential content is shared only with specific people, never with a link for the whole organization, and never outside the company without approval under GOV-10.
  • P-08-05Basic Passwords, access keys, payment card numbers, and personal data are not written into chat or email and are not stored in unprotected documents. Passwords belong in the [company password manager], personal data in a document labeled Confidential on a site designated for that purpose.
  • P-08-06Basic Email is communication, not storage. A document from an email that is to remain is saved to the location according to the matrix; email is retained under GOV-12.
  • P-08-07Basic The local drive, USB, private clouds, and private email are not used for company documents. Offline work takes place through OneDrive sync on a managed device.
  • P-08-08Basic When an employee leaves, their OneDrive passes to their manager; the company keeps it for [90 days] and then deletes it. Before leaving, the employee moves shared documents to Teams or SharePoint.
  • P-08-09Standard On a mobile device, company documents are handled only in Microsoft 365 apps (Teams, OneDrive, SharePoint, Office) on a device registered with the company. Other apps do not open or download company content.

sections.title: 4. Procedures
sections.html:
4. Procedures

4.1 Where to save a new document

  1. The user answers the question "What is it?": a draft or a note for myself belongs in OneDrive or OneNote; a team's working document in a Teams channel; an approved or official document on the department site or the intranet.
  2. The user answers the question "For whom?": only for me means OneDrive; for the team, Teams; for the department or the whole company, SharePoint; for people outside the company, an external collaboration site under GOV-10, never OneDrive.
  3. The user answers the question "How long?": days or weeks mean OneDrive or Teams; years or "as long as it is valid" mean SharePoint with the metadata filled in.
  4. When in doubt, the user saves the document to a Teams channel or asks the site owner; the "Save document" guide in My Documents selects the library according to the matrix.

4.2 How to share correctly

  1. The user first saves the document to the location according to the matrix; from OneDrive, the user shares only drafts and only for a limited time.
  2. In the Share dialog, the user keeps "Specific people" and selects the permission: View as the default, Edit only for co-authors.
  3. The user inserts the link into Teams or an email. An attachment is used only for recipients outside Microsoft 365 and only for Public or Internal documents.
  4. For a document labeled Confidential, the user verifies that it is shared only inside the company; external sharing is handled by the site owner under GOV-10.
  5. After the collaboration ends, the user removes the access in the Manage access window.

4.3 What to do before leaving a project

  1. The user goes through their OneDrive and moves the documents the project or team needs to a Teams channel or a site library; the copies in OneDrive are deleted.
  2. The user hands over ownership of documents, lists, and Power Automate flows to a successor or the site owner.
  3. The user transcribes conclusions from OneNote and Loop into documents in the library and ends sharing that is no longer needed.
  4. The site owner confirms the takeover of the documents. When leaving the company, the manager takes over the OneDrive under P-08-08.

Tools

Microsoft 365: OneDrive, Teams, SharePoint, Loop, and OneNote; the Share dialog and the Manage access window. EP365: My Documents shows the user all documents they have access to, and the "Save document" guide selects the library according to the matrix and fills in the metadata; Quick Actions provides a direct link, PDF, print, email, and a sensitive-data check in the library menu; Managed Documents releases this policy to employees with acknowledgment.
